transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-30 14:00 PST | Duration: 45m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CSM) -- Alicia Gomez (Oceanside Head of ML), Tom Rivera (Platform Eng), Priya Menon (Security), Marco Silva (Data)
---
[00:00] Jordan Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, super excited to walk through the Console usage analytics and the per route cost breakdown today. quick agenda: dashboards, cost + routing, then Q&A - and we'll capture next steps.
[00:18] Alicia Gomez: Thanks Jordan, we're keen to see how Redwood can give us per-route visibility; our ops teams keep asking for "who is costing what" at token level, so show us how that looks.
[00:34] Maya Chen: Great, I'll share my screen -- tiny note, deck and console link are in the meeting chat (Deck: console-usage-analytics.pdf, Bench: redwood-bench.xlsx).
[00:48] [screen noise] Maya Chen: Alright top left is the usage overview -- tokens in, tokens out, 95th pct latency, and error rate. You can filter by model, route, and time window.
[01:10] Tom Rivera: Can you filter by customer tenant? we run multiple brands under Oceanside and need cost-back to brand.
[01:22] Maya Chen: Yep--you can tag routes by tenant id or product line, and the per-route dashboard will show cost and token counts attributed to that tag. Filtering is immediate, for long windows we async aggregate.
[01:40] Alicia Gomez: How precise is the cost number? is it a rough estimate or bill-accurate?
[01:49] Maya Chen: It's modeled using your provisioning + kernel costs + token compute. For hosted we show estimated unit cost with breakdown (GPU time, infra, egress). For Dedicated we can ingest your committed capacity and show amortized cost. it's within a few percent for most workloads but we recommend running the pilot for bill-accurate validation.
[02:12] [slight crosstalk] Priya Menon: Quick security question - the audit logs, retention and SSO -- can we keep console logs in our S3 and tie to our KMS?
[02:24] Liam O'Connor: Yes, Private / VPC and Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and logs to S3. We'll share the SOC 2 and VPC deployment docs after.
[02:37] Maya Chen: Back to dashboards -- this per-route view shows route latency distribution, percentile tails, tokens per request histogram, and cost per 1,000 tokens. You can drill into a route's recent requests and replay sample payloads for debugging.
[03:05] Marco Silva: Do you support annotating requests for business metrics? like connect route to revenue_source tag?
[03:13] Maya Chen: Absolutely - request metadata can carry business tags, and cost/usage can be grouped by those tags. it's very helpful for chargeback.
[03:28] Jordan Park: One thing customers love is the per-model and per-route cost delta. for example you can see switching from a 7B quantized model to an 13B fp16 variant and the delta per route.
[03:45] Alicia Gomez: We have a mix of short queries and long chat sessions - latency vs cost tradeoff is key for us. how do you recommend setting SLOs?
[03:58] Maya Chen: We surface P95 and P99 latency; you can set budget-based routing so latency-sensitive routes go to Dedicated or low-latency pool, and cheaper routes go to a batched pool. The console has routing policies you can apply per-route.
[04:20] Tom Rivera: About Dedicated - what's the minimum commitment and burst options?
[04:27] Jordan Park: Typical minimum starts at a few GPUs per month for early pilots; we can do burst capacity for traffic spikes. I'll include a few contract examples in the pricing doc.
[04:38] [background typing] Priya Menon: On compliance - do you provide per-token redaction or PII scrubbing before logs hit storage?
[04:47] Maya Chen: We have configurable scrubbing at the edge and can redact sensitive fields before storing logs; plus you can route raw logs to your VPC for in-house scrubbing.
[05:02] Marco Silva: Can we see a live example of a route cost breakdown?
[05:07] Maya Chen: Sure, pulling up Route: /search/products. See here: traffic distribution, tokens per call avg 120, 1k-token cost $0.45 on hosted t-optim profile; on Dedicated amortized cost is $0.18 assuming your committed pool.
[05:32] Alicia Gomez: That delta is interesting. how do you handle KV cache or prefix caching in cost calc? we heavily use cache to reduce tokens.
[05:44] Maya Chen: Good point - the console factors cache hit rates into effective token counts. if a request hits the KV cache, we attribute lower compute token usage and show effective cost per request after cache savings.
[06:05] Jordan Park: Also worth noting we expose model variant fallbacks; if capacity constrained we can route to a compatible quantized variant automatically and the console will show the quality delta if you upload evals.
[06:24] Tom Rivera: We need to run an in-house benchmark comparing our current infra - we want to validate latency for our 2k token sessions.
[06:33] Maya Chen: We have a benchmark template (redwood-bench.xlsx) and a runbook. I'll share scripts that run 2k token sessions and collect P95/P99.
[06:46] Priya Menon: Are network egress costs visible? we pay a lot for cross-region egress.
[06:54] Maya Chen: Yes, egress is shown separately. in Dedicated or Private deployment we can show true egress costs based on your cloud pricing if you provide the rates.
[07:08] [screen scroll] Maya Chen: Next section is Alerts and Anomalies - you can set alerts on token spike, cost drift per route, or quality regression.
[07:25] Marco Silva: Does anomaly detection support custom metrics?
[07:29] Maya Chen: You can feed custom metrics via our ingest API and then tie them to alerts and dashboards.
[07:38] Jordan Park: Let's talk about cost allocation for multi-tenant. you can tag requests with tenant id and then run cost reports that produce monthly chargeback CSVs.
[07:52] Alicia Gomez: That's exactly what our finance team asked for - automated chargebacks. can you export to our billing system?
[07:58] Jordan Park: We support CSV, S3 dump, and direct connectors (we've done integrations with a few billing systems).
[08:08] Tom Rivera: About model catalog - do you curate recommended quantization profiles per model?
[08:14] Maya Chen: Yes we recommend quantization and kernel selection per architecture; you'll see recommended profiles on the model details page along with perf/cost estimates.
[08:30] [brief pause] Alicia Gomez: On the hosted side - what SLAs are available? we need 99.9% for our customer-facing features.
[08:38] Jordan Park: Hosted has tiered SLAs; for higher SLOs we recommend Dedicated with SLA-backed pools. we'll include specifics in the contract examples.
[08:48] Priya Menon: For Private deployment - can we manage keys in HSM and have audit logs shipped to our SIEM?
[08:57] Liam O'Connor: Yes, HSM/KMS integrations supported and logs can be exported to SIEM via S3 or streaming. We'll include the architecture diagram in follow-up.
[09:10] Maya Chen: Switching to the Cost Explorer view - it's similar to cloud cost explorers but at token/granularity. you can show trend lines, top N routes by spend, and drill to model+route combos.
[09:35] Marco Silva: Can we simulate price changes to see impact?
[09:38] Maya Chen: There's a "what-if" slider to change per-token cost or GPU amortization and see projected monthly bill changes.
[09:48] Tom Rivera: We have a question about blended workloads - half our calls are short intent lookups, half are long summarizations - can you show blended per-route cost?
[09:57] Maya Chen: yes the console will compute weighted averages based on observed distribution; you can also create synthetic mixes in the benchmark template.
[10:08] [timestamp jump to mid-call] [21:12] Jordan Park: Recap so far: Alicia/Tom want per-route cost and chargeback to brands, Priya wants SOC 2/VPC details and PII scrubbing, we agreed on a pilot to validate costs and latency.
[21:28] Alicia Gomez: Sounds right. for the pilot, we'd like to test 2k token sessions at our peak qps and measure P95/P99 over 1 week.
[21:36] Maya Chen: That works. We'll propose pilot configuration: 2 GPU Dedicated pool, 1-week run, synthetic and replayed real traffic.
[21:46] Tom Rivera: For replaying traffic, we'll need small changes to payloads to remove PII - is that supported?
[21:52] Maya Chen: Yes we provide helpers to scrub and replay safely.
[22:02] Priya Menon: Who signs the NDA and what data handling terms? we have strict vendor rules.
[22:08] Liam O'Connor: We'll share a standard DPA and security packet. our legal team can start a redline if needed.
[22:17] Jordan Park: Demo: quick toggle -- here is cost-per-route heatmap, click any cell to see the list of requests sampled. you can export those samples or send to S3.
[22:39] Marco Silva: Any integrations with our observability stack? we use Datadog and Sentry.
[22:45] Maya Chen: We have tracing hooks and exporters; we've shipped Datadog dashboards and Sentry error hooks before.
[22:58] [small lag] Jordan Park: One last feature: Quality monitoring - connect a golden prompt set and the console will run periodic evals and send regression alerts.
[23:14] Alicia Gomez: That's a big one for product - we need guardrails so a model swap doesn't quietly degrade UX.
[23:22] Maya Chen: Exactly - and those evals can be tied to rollout policies so you can auto-fallback.
[23:32] Tom Rivera: Ok what's the timeline if we want a pilot next week?
[23:36] Jordan Park: If you send traffic profile and the sample data today, we can stand up a pilot cluster within 72 hours; bench scripts run for 1 week.
[23:47] Alicia Gomez: We'll aim to provide the traffic profile and tenant tags by Dec 1.
[23:52] Jordan Park: Perfect. final recap and next steps coming in the notes. thanks all, we'll follow up with pricing, SOC2 pack, and benchmark runbook.
[24:05] [00:24 onwards - wrap up chatter and meeting ends with thanks]
